questions.question: Which of the following best describes the effect of forces on an object?

options.A: They can only change the object's position.
options.B: They can only change the object's speed.
options.C: They can change the object's size and shape.
options.D: They have no effect on the object's size or shape.

questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): They can change the object's size and shape.. A force can change the motion, direction, speed, size, or shape of an object. When force is applied, deformation may occur. Objects like rubber bands stretch under force. Therefore, force can change size and shape.

questions.question: The balance wheel in a mechanical clock uses Hooke's law to:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Measure time precisely. Hooke’s Law relates force and extension in springs. The balance wheel oscillates due to spring restoring force. These regular oscillations measure equal time intervals. Hence it helps in precise time measurement.

questions.question: The elastic limit indicates:

options.A: The maximum load a material can handle
options.B: The point beyond which Hooke's law no longer applies
options.C: The point where the material returns to its original shape
options.D: The elastic limit of the material

questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): The elastic limit of the material. Elastic limit is the maximum limit of elastic behavior. Beyond this point, the material does not return to original shape. Hooke’s Law is valid only within elastic limit. After crossing it, permanent deformation occurs.

questions.question: If the load-extension graph of an elastic solid starts to curve and deviate from linearity, it indicates:

options.A: The material has crossed its elastic limit
options.B: The material is still in its purely elastic region
options.D: The material has not been deformed

questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): The material has crossed its elastic limit. A straight line graph shows Hooke’s Law is obeyed. When the graph curves, proportionality ends. This means elastic limit is exceeded. Material enters plastic region.

questions.question: If the force is constant, what happens to pressure as area increases?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Pressure decreases. Pressure = Force / Area. If force remains constant and area increases, the value of pressure decreases. Hence pressure and area are inversely proportional.

questions.question: If you push down on the top of a sealed syringe filled with water, in which direction is the force exerted by the water on the syringe's sides?

options.C: Sideways, at right angles to the surface
options.D: In the direction of the push

questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): In the direction of the push. According to Pascal’s Law, pressure acts equally in all directions. It acts perpendicular to surfaces. The push is transmitted throughout the fluid. Thus force is exerted in the direction of push and all sides.

questions.question: A balloon expands uniformly in all directions when pressed. This demonstrates that the force due to pressure in a fluid is:

options.A: Directed towards the bottom of the balloon only
options.B: Greatest at the sides of the balloon
options.C: Exerted equally in all directions at right angles to the surface
options.D: Non-existent as air cannot exert force

questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Exerted equally in all directions at right angles to the surface. Fluid pressure acts equally in all directions. It always acts perpendicular to surfaces. This is why balloon expands uniformly. It proves Pascal’s principle of pressure transmission.

questions.question: Which of the following phenomena justifies that the atmosphere exerts pressure?

options.A: A balloon deflating when taken to a higher altitude
options.B: A balloon inflating more at higher altitudes
options.C: A vacuum not affecting the shape of a balloon

questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Collapse of crushed can when air is pumped out. The collapsing can experiment is the standard demonstration in FBISE Physics 9: when air inside a sealed tin can is removed, surrounding atmospheric pressure crushes it.

questions.question: What happens to atmospheric pressure as an airplane ascends to cruising altitude?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): It decreases. Atmospheric pressure decreases with height. Air density becomes lower at higher altitudes. Less air above means less pressure. Therefore pressure decreases as plane ascends.

questions.question: How might a change in atmospheric pressure be indicative of approaching weather?

options.A: A significant drop in pressure suggests clear skies
options.B: An increase in pressure indicates a storm
options.C: A sudden increase in pressure signals rain
options.D: A drop in pressure often precedes the arrival of a storm

questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): A drop in pressure often precedes the arrival of a storm. A rapid fall in atmospheric pressure indicates an approaching low-pressure storm system with wind and rain.

questions.question: What happens to the liquid level in a barometer when atmospheric pressure increases?

options.C: The liquid level does not change

questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): The liquid level rises. Barometer liquid rises when pressure increases. More atmospheric force pushes down on the liquid reservoir. This pushes liquid up the tube. Hence liquid level indicates pressure change.

questions.question: How does the pressure of water at 10 m compare to that at 5 m depth?

options.D: It is four times as much

questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): It is twice as much. Pressure in a liquid = ρgh If depth doubles, pressure doubles. So at 10 m, pressure is twice the 5 m depth. Pressure increases linearly with depth.

questions.question: If the density of a liquid is increased but depth remains the same, what happens to pressure?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): The pressure increases. Pressure in liquid = ρgh If ρ (density) increases while h and g are constant, pressure increases proportionally. Denser liquids exert more pressure at the same depth.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a manometer?

options.B: To measure pressure of a fluid

questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): To measure pressure of a fluid. A manometer measures fluid pressure. It shows difference between atmospheric and fluid pressure. Used in labs, industries, and HVAC systems. Pressure reading is indicated by liquid height difference.

questions.question: In hydraulic brakes, force is transmitted:

options.C: As increased pressure through brake fluid

questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): As increased pressure through brake fluid. Hydraulic brakes use Pascal’s law. Small pedal force creates pressure in brake fluid. This pressure is transmitted to all brakes equally. Hence brakes amplify force effectively.

questions.question: Pressure is determined as:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Force divided by area. Pressure is defined as the normal force per unit area (P = F / A).

questions.question: Which unit is pressure measured in?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Pascal. The SI unit of pressure is the Pascal (Pa), equivalent to 1 N/m².

questions.question: If a force of 50 N is applied on an area of 0.005 m², the pressure is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 10,000 Pa. Pressure = Force / Area = 50 / 0.005 = 10,000 Pa Pressure depends inversely on area. Smaller area → higher pressure. Hence correct pressure = 10,000 Pa.

questions.question: When you blow up a balloon, pressure acts:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Outwards in all directions. Air inside the balloon exerts pressure equally in all directions. This is due to fluid (gas) pressure acting perpendicular to the surface. Hence balloon expands uniformly. Shows Pascal’s principle in gases.

questions.question: A sudden fall in barometer reading indicates:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): A storm is likely. A sudden drop in barometric pressure signals an impending storm or cyclone.

questions.question: If atmospheric pressure increases, mercury level in a barometer:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Rises. More atmospheric pressure pushes mercury higher in the tube. Barometer measures air pressure. Higher air weight → higher mercury column. Hence liquid level rises with increased pressure.

questions.question: If depth in water is doubled, pressure:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Doubles. Pressure in liquid = ρgh Doubling depth doubles pressure. Pressure depends linearly on depth. Hence deeper water → more pressure.

questions.question: A manometer measures:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Pressure. A manometer is a U-tube instrument specifically designed to measure fluid (gas or liquid) pressure.

questions.question: Which industry heavily uses manometers?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Chemical processing. Chemical plants require precise pressure measurement. Manometers monitor gases and liquids in pipelines. Safety and efficiency depend on accurate pressure readings. Hence chemical industry uses them widely.

questions.question: Practical use of Pascal’s Law in vehicles:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Hydraulic brakes. Hydraulic brakes amplify pedal force using brake fluid. Pressure is transmitted undiminished to all brakes. Allows small effort to stop vehicle effectively. This is a direct application of Pascal’s Law.

questions.question: If density of mercury = 13600 kg/m³ and height = 0.05 m, pressure difference is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 6800 Pa. Pressure = ρgh = 13600 × 9.8 × 0.05 ≈ 6800 Pa Shows direct relationship between density, gravity, and height. This formula is used in barometers and manometers. Hence pressure difference = 6800 Pa.

questions.question: Rapid increase in atmospheric pressure is linked with:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Clear skies. High-pressure systems are associated with calm, clear weather. Rapid rise indicates incoming stable air. Low-pressure system causes storms. Hence increasing pressure → clear skies.

questions.question: Liquid pressure depends on:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Depth of liquid. By hydrostatic pressure law P = ρgh, liquid pressure depends directly on the depth (h) beneath the surface and the density of the liquid.

questions.question: Rising of liquid in a barometer tube indicates:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Increasing atmospheric pressure. Barometer liquid rises when atmospheric pressure increases. More air weight pushes the liquid higher. It measures pressure variations accurately. Hence rising liquid = higher pressure.

questions.question: Greatest water pressure is experienced when:

options.B: Diving to bottom of deep pool

questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Diving to bottom of deep pool. Hydrostatic pressure increases linearly with depth (P = ρgh); therefore, maximum pressure is experienced at the greatest depth.

questions.question: Main feature of elastic deformation:

options.C: Returns to original shape after force is removed

questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Returns to original shape after force is removed. Elastic deformation is temporary. Once applied force is removed, material returns to original shape. Hooke’s Law applies in elastic region. Permanent changes occur only after elastic limit is exceeded.

questions.question: According to Hooke’s Law, spring constant (k):

options.B: Force required to extend spring by 1 m

questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Force required to extend spring by 1 m. Spring constant (k) = F / x It shows how stiff the spring is. Higher k → more force needed to stretch. Units: N/m.

questions.question: When deformation exceeds elastic limit:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Permanent deformation occurs. Elastic limit = maximum reversible deformation. Exceeding it causes permanent shape change. Hooke’s Law no longer applies. Material does not return to original shape.

questions.question: Area under load-extension graph represents:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Energy absorbed. Work done = force × extension In physics, the area under a graph represents the product of the two axes. For a load-extension graph (Force vs. Distance): Work Done: When you apply a force to stretch a material, you are doing “work” on it. Energy Absorbed: That work doesn’t disappear; it is stored in the material as Elastic Potential Energy. Because the work done by the external force is equal to the energy absorbed by the object, both terms are technically correct.

questions.question: Stretching experiment tests:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Elastic limit and spring constant. Load-extension experiments test the elastic properties of a material, determining its spring constant (k) and elastic limit.

questions.question: A galvanometer works by:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Hooke’s Law. Current in coil creates magnetic field. Interaction with permanent magnet deflects needle. Deflection proportional to current. Hooke’s Law helps restore needle to zero.

questions.question: Elastic and plastic deformation differ because:

options.B: Elastic is temporary, plastic is permanent

questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Elastic is temporary, plastic is permanent. Elastic deformation disappears after removing force. Plastic deformation remains permanent. Materials may show both types under different forces. Key in engineering and material design.

questions.question: The first man who came up with the idea of gravity was:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Issac Newton. Isaac Newton formulated the universal law of gravitation. He explained that every body attracts every other body. He also related this force to the motion of planets. Newton’s laws of motion and gravitation laid the foundation of classical mechanics.

questions.question: A force due to which every body of the universe attracts every other body is called:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Gravitational force. Gravitational force acts between any two masses. It is always attractive and acts along the line joining their centers. It is universal and applies to all objects. Other forces like magnetic or electric are not universal for all masses.

questions.question: Force of gravitation is inversely proportional to:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Square of distance. Newton's law of universal gravitation states that gravitational attraction is inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers (inverse-square law, F ∝ 1/r²).

questions.question: Gravitational force is directly proportional to:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Mass. Larger masses attract each other more strongly. F = G (m₁ m₂)/r² shows direct proportionality to m₁ and m₂. If either mass doubles, force doubles. This explains why Earth’s gravity is strong due to its large mass.

questions.question: If the distance between two masses is halved then the force of gravitation becomes:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Four times. Force ∝ 1/r² Halving r → force increases by (1/½)² = 4 times. Smaller distance → stronger attraction. This principle applies to satellites and planets.

questions.question: Law of gravitation is consistent with:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Newton’s 3rd law of motion. The gravitational attraction between two masses forms an action-reaction pair: body A attracts body B with a force equal in magnitude and opposite in direction to the force with which body B attracts body A (Newton's 3rd law).

questions.question: Gravitational force of attraction between two objects is not felt by us because of:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Small masses. Because the universal gravitational constant G is exceedingly small (6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m²/kg²), the gravitational force between everyday objects with small masses is far too weak to be perceived.

questions.question: Gravitational force per unit mass is known as:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Gravitational field strength. Gravitational field strength = force per unit mass. Symbol: g, unit N/kg It indicates how much force a mass experiences at a point. It is different from potential energy.

questions.question: The acceleration due to gravity on the surface of moon is 1.62 m/s². The radius of moon is 1740 km. Mass of moon is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 7.35 × 10²² kg. g = G M / R² → M = g R² / G Substitute g = 1.62 m/s², R = 1.74 × 10⁶ m, G = 6.673 × 10⁻¹¹ Calculation gives 7.35 × 10²² kg Mass depends on acceleration and radius.

questions.question: SI unit of gravitational field strength is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): N/kg. Gravitational field strength g = F/m Unit: N/kg = m/s² Thus all given units are valid It shows force per unit mass or acceleration.

questions.question: If mass of a body on the surface of earth is m, then its weight on the surface of moon is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 1.62 m. Weight on Moon = m × gₘ gₘ = 1.62 m/s², gₑ = 9.81 m/s² Weight ratio = gₘ / gₑ ≈ 0.165 Hence weight on Moon ≈ 0.16 m Body weighs less on Moon due to smaller g.

questions.question: If weight of a body on the surface of earth is B, its weight on the moon will be:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): 1/6 B. The acceleration due to gravity on the Moon is roughly one-sixth of that on Earth (g_m ≈ g_e / 6), so weight on the Moon is B / 6.

questions.question: An object is placed at height three Earth radii. The value of g at that height will be:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 1/16 g. At altitude h = 3R, the distance from the Earth's center is r = R + 3R = 4R. Since g ∝ 1/r², g' = g / (4)² = g / 16.

questions.question: If mass of two bodies is 2 kg and distance between their centers is 1 m, then the gravitational force between them is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 4G. According to Newton's law: F = G (m₁ m₂) / r² = G (2 × 2) / (1)² = 4G.

questions.question: GPS consists of ___ earth satellites:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): 24. Global Positioning System uses 24 satellites. Orbits ensure at least 4 satellites visible from any location. Allows accurate position and time determination. Additional satellites improve precision and coverage.

questions.question: GPS satellites revolve around the earth ___ in a day:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 2 times. GPS satellites operate in Medium Earth Orbit (MEO) with an orbital period of approximately 12 hours, completing 2 full revolutions around the Earth every 24 hours.

questions.question: The speed of GPS satellite is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 3.87 km/s. Orbital speed v = √(GM / r) For GPS orbit (~20,200 km above Earth), v ≈ 3.87 km/s This ensures stable circular orbit. Higher or lower speed disrupts orbit.

questions.question: Moon is nearly ___ away from the earth:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): 380,000 km. Average distance Earth–Moon ≈ 384,000 km Used in calculating gravitational effects, tides, and satellite motion. Expressed in km or megameters (Mm). Distance allows Moon to orbit Earth steadily.

questions.question: Moon completes its one revolution around the earth in:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): All of them. All units correspond to same period: ~27.3 days Moon’s revolution period is sidereal month. Used for calendar and tidal calculations. Hence all units are valid.

questions.question: Relative velocity of geostationary satellite with respect to earth is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Zero. Geostationary satellites orbit with Earth’s rotation. From surface, satellite appears stationary. Hence relative velocity = 0 km/s. Used for TV, weather, and communication.

questions.question: The orbital speed of a low orbit satellite is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 8 km/s. Low Earth orbit satellites move ~8 km/s. High enough to balance gravity and centrifugal force. Maintains circular orbit close to Earth. Speed ensures satellite doesn’t fall or escape.

questions.question: Mass of the earth is measured by:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): R² g / G. From g = G M / R², solving for Earth's mass gives M = g R² / G.

questions.question: Mass of Earth is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 6 × 10²⁴ kg. To calculate the Earth’s mass (M), we use the formula for the acceleration of gravity (g) at the surface: g=GxM/R2 By rearranging it to solve for M: M = gR²/G The Values: * g (Gravity): 9.8 m/s² * R (Earth’s Radius): 6,400,000 meters (6.4 × 10⁶ m) * G (Gravitational Constant): 6.67 × 10-11 The Result: When you plug these numbers in: M = (9.8) x (6.4x10⁶)²/6.67x10-11 This gives approximately 6 × 1024kg.

questions.question: The value of gravitational field strength on the surface of the Moon is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): 1.62 N/kg. Moon’s g ≈ 1.62 m/s² = 1.62 N/kg Gravitational field strength = force per unit mass Much smaller than Earth’s g (9.81 N/kg) Causes objects to weigh less on Moon.

questions.question: The orbital speed of a satellite revolving very close to the Earth is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): √(g R). Orbital speed v = √(G M / R) = √(g R) for near-Earth orbit Depends on Earth’s gravity and radius Ensures satellite remains in circular orbit Higher speed → satellite escapes, lower speed → it falls.

questions.question: A satellite revolves around the Earth due to:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): Gravitational force. The gravitational attraction between the Earth and the satellite provides the required centripetal force for orbital motion.

questions.question: Gravitational force on Earth’s surface is equal to:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): All of them. Earth’s surface gravity can be expressed in various units All values represent the same force per unit mass Depends on measurement unit used N/kg, m/s², or cm/s² are equivalent.

questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'Force / Area'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 5 (Pressure & Deformation in Solids), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Pascal’s Law states:

options.A: Pressure is transmitted equally in all directions

questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 'Pressure is transmitted equally in all directions'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 5 (Pressure & Deformation in Solids), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: A sharp knife cuts better because:

options.B: Area is less, so pressure is more

questions.question: Pressure in liquids acts:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 'In all directions'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 5 (Pressure & Deformation in Solids), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: The SI unit of stress is same as:

questions.question: Strain is defined as:

questions.question: Young’s Modulus is the ratio of:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 'Stress to Strain'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 5 (Pressure & Deformation in Solids), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: The greater the Young’s Modulus:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'More rigid the material is'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 5 (Pressure & Deformation in Solids), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: A rubber band has:

questions.question: Compressive stress:

questions.question: Tensile stress:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'Increases length'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 5 (Pressure & Deformation in Solids), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Which of the following materials is most elastic?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'Steel'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 5 (Pressure & Deformation in Solids), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: The ability of a material to return to its original shape is called:

questions.question: Stress and strain are both caused by:

questions.question: The force that tends to deform a body is called:

questions.question: Breaking point is the point where:

questions.question: Which of the following has the highest pressure on the ground?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'Needle's tip'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 5 (Pressure & Deformation in Solids), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: The shape of a dam is wider at the base because:

options.B: Water pressure is higher at the bottom

questions.question: When stress exceeds elastic limit:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'Permanent deformation occurs'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 5 (Pressure & Deformation in Solids), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: The dimensional formula of pressure is:

questions.question: A small area increases pressure because:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 'Force is concentrated'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 5 (Pressure & Deformation in Solids), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: The change in shape of a body under stress is called:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 'Deformation'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 5 (Pressure & Deformation in Solids), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: If a force of 200 N is applied on an area of 2 m², pressure will be:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): '100 Pa'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 5 (Pressure & Deformation in Solids), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: A body with high elasticity has:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'High Young's modulus'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 5 (Pressure & Deformation in Solids), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Which is a scalar quantity?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 'Pressure'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 5 (Pressure & Deformation in Solids), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: The change in volume per unit volume is called:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 'Volume strain'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 5 (Pressure & Deformation in Solids), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: When force is applied parallel to surface, it produces:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'Shear stress'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 5 (Pressure & Deformation in Solids), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Tensile and compressive stress are types of:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 'Normal stress'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 5 (Pressure & Deformation in Solids), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a factor affecting pressure in solids?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'Volume'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 5 (Pressure & Deformation in Solids), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.
